A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E. Content can be matched reliably across the layout changes and figure renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original OpenML feature analysis, repeated convergence experiments on synthetic and HTTP/SMTP data, and calculated depth examples for generated datasets.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds featurewise convergence experiments on Iris in Section 5.1 and Figure 5(b).

M1.justification: v2 removes Section 6's auxiliary multidimensional depth-estimation recipes: averaging coordinatewise expected depths and evaluating depths after a one-dimensional feature mapping. The iForest procedure in Algorithms 1–3 and the k-NN scoring rule remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Section 5.1 adds Iris measurements to the featurewise convergence evaluation, extending the represented data domain. The synthetic distributions, HTTP/SMTP datasets, OpenML analysis, and generated anomaly examples are retained; Iris classification is not evaluated.

E2.justification: The iForest versus k-NN comparisons in the case studies and Table 2 retain the same methods. EIF replaces OptIForest only in the background discussion, without adding or removing an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The convergence protocol retains featurewise one-dimensional evaluation, mean squared error, 100 subsamples, and 100–1000 trees; Iris follows this same protocol. Section 5.2 still uses datasets of 20 independently sampled uniform points.

E4.justification: Section 6 replaces the multidimensional reduction illustrations with diagnostic toy cases examining point arrangements, changing split candidates, and whether subset decomposition and coordinate averaging remain exact. The original one-dimensional analytical cases and empirical depth examples remain.

E5.justification: v1 Figure 3 explicitly identifies shaded regions as 95% confidence regions; corresponding v2 Figure 5 omits the confidence level. Both versions retain 10 independent repetitions, so this is reduced reporting specificity rather than evidence of changed run counts.

E6.justification: v2 Figure 5(b) adds convergence curves for four Iris features. The previous synthetic, HTTP, and SMTP curves and generated depth examples are retained, as are Table 1's counts of 930,738 successful, 930,751 valid, and 933,440 total features.

T1.justification: v2 adds Proposition 6.1: a four-point counterexample gives 745/288 versus 744/288 for subset decomposition and 491/288 versus 492/288 for coordinate averaging. Appendix A also contains localized corrections, including expectation scaling in A.1 and applying linearity to expected depth in A.5. The original one-dimensional theorem statements and substantive arguments in Appendices B–E remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's two listed contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: random-walk characterization and expected-depth analysis, lower sensitivity to central anomalies, and greater parameter adaptability than k-NN.

C2.justification: v1 Section 6 asserts that projection or kernel mapping allows all Section 4 conclusions to apply in multiple dimensions. v2 replaces this applicability argument with explicit obstacles and failures of particular exact reductions, and presents multidimensional bounds as future work. This substantially narrows the interpretation of the theory's reach.

D1.justification: The new checklist directs readers to supplemental code, data, reproduction instructions, training details, and computing infrastructure information. These are new access statements; the supplied PDFs contain neither that supplement nor a code link, so actual availability and the additional details cannot be verified.

R1.justification: v2 adds Fisher (1936), Bhattacharya and Waymire (2021), and Hariri et al. (2021, EIF), while removing Xiang et al. (2023, OptIForest). These are limited background changes; the central novelty positioning remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and several explanatory paragraphs are rewritten, the random-walk explanation is expanded, and 'density factor' becomes 'density ratio.' Section 6 receives a new internal structure and a checklist is added, while the overall section sequence and most exposition remain.

P2.justification: The main text switches from single to double columns, with extensive figure and algorithm repositioning. Figure 1 gains two illustrated trajectories; original Figure 2 is separated into Figures 2–4; convergence panels are rearranged around the added Iris panel; depth examples are stacked; and the original multidimensional Figure 5 is replaced by new Figures 7–8.

improvement.justification: The strongest gain is Section 6's replacement of blanket multidimensional applicability with explicit limitations and a concrete counterexample to particular exact reductions. Local proof corrections and the Iris check provide smaller benefits. Most core theory and empirical evidence remain unchanged, while omission of the 95% confidence level reduces reporting precision. The checklist's promised supplemental details cannot be assessed from these PDFs. Overall, the more careful treatment of scope supports a limited net improvement.
